key_insight: LLM agents can improve crystal-structure determination from powder X-ray diffraction by searching candidate structures and verifying their simulated diffraction profiles.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support self-driving materials laboratories by improving automated characterization without requiring a collection of solved experimental measurements.
method: Search candidate structures using forward-simulated profile agreement as an inference-time verifier.
Adapt agents and use repeated sampling with verifier-guided inference-time scaling.
Evolve persistent guidance and executable tools by diagnosing failures on synthetic problems, then transfer them to measured patterns.
evidence_signal: On the 200-problem simulated pXRD-Bench, agent adaptation raised selected structural recovery from 27% to 69%; on 15 measured patterns, the evolved package improved average profile agreement.
watch_item: Experimental evaluation covers only 15 measured patterns, and improved profile agreement alone does not establish correct structure recovery.
paper_title: Verifiable pXRD: Hill-climbing pXRD structure determination with LLM agents
